message.content:
The reflection line is the angle bisector between  
\[
\begin{pmatrix}5\\0\end{pmatrix}\quad\text{and}\quad \begin{pmatrix}4\\3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Since \((4,3)\) has angle whose cosine is \(4/5\) and sine is \(3/5\), the reflection line has half that angle, so a unit direction vector for the line is
\[
\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}},\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\right).
\]

For reflection across a line with unit direction \(d\), the formula is
\[
R(v)=2(d\cdot v)d-v.
\]
Let
\[
v=\begin{pmatrix}-2\\3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
d\cdot v=\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}},\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\right)\cdot(-2,3)
=\frac{-6+3}{\sqrt{10}}=-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}.
\]
So
\[
2(d\cdot v)d
=2\left(-\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\right)\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}},\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\right)
=\left(-\frac{9}{5},-\frac{3}{5}\right).
\]
Thus
\[
R(v)=\left(-\frac{9}{5},-\frac{3}{5}\right)-(-2,3)
=\left(\frac{1}{5},-\frac{18}{5}\right).
\]

The answer is \(\begin{pmatrix}\frac{1}{5}\\ -\frac{18}{5}\end{pmatrix}\).
